correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2 the categorical (tensor/direct, not Cartesian) graph C7 x Kn has edges precisely across adjacent cycle rows of unequal colors. Matching the least available color-0 row in each Boolean fiber leaves an upper order filter of color-0-free faces with total-dominating row support. Such faces consist of at most two monochromatic occupied runs, with cover relations preserving the exact remaining color set, hence disjoint one- and two-color sectors independent of n. Reconstructed the complete seven-letter 2^7/3^7 word filters: respectively 29 and 28 faces; checked their greedy Hasse orientations for acyclicity, their critical words (1,1,0,0,1,1,1) in degree 4 and (1,1,0,2,2,0,0)/(0,2,2,2,0,1,1) in degrees 3/4, and exact integer top Morse boundary zero (not merely modulo 2). Each one-color sector contributes a degree-4 cell and each two-color sector a degree-3 and degree-4 cell; upper-filter separation makes every other top differential zero. The resulting 2-connected Morse CW model has cells only in dimensions 0,3,4; Hurewicz π3≅H3 identifies zero integral attaching degrees with nullhomotopic maps, proving Ind(C7 x Kn) ≃ wedge^{binom(n-1,2)} S3 vee wedge^{binom(n,2)} S4. n=2 has zero three-cells and one four-cell. Full-complex checks n=2..5 are corroboration, not the all-n step: it is justified by fixed sectors.

value.rationale: An exact all-color integral homotopy classification for the seven-cycle categorical graph product addresses a published torsion question, not a routine one-off example. Uniform 29/28-state reduction provides a reusable structural mechanism and exact binomial Betti multiplicities for an infinite family; the integer cancellation eliminates potential Moore summands. The result does not resolve arbitrary cycle lengths or equivariant modules.
